required_outcomes: Treats the case as an emergency or urgent security repair (window cannot be shut or locked, opens onto a communal walkway, attempted break-in overnight), not as a routine chase.

Replies to the tenant promptly with safety advice and an honest plan: call 999 if anyone tries again, keep the bedroom door shut, a same-day make-safe is being arranged (no time promised until confirmed), and asks whether she has somewhere safe to sleep tonight.

Arranges a same-day make-safe (temporary lock, securing or boarding) without waiting for the landlord; because Oscar Turner has not answered three reminders and no other contractor is on file, escalates to a human with priority to source an emergency locksmith or glazier today.
Informs the landlord of the attempted break-in, the crime reference and the emergency make-safe, as a notification rather than a request for permission.
acceptable_alternatives: Phoning Oscar Turner first and, if he can attend today, booking him for the make-safe, provided the escalation still happens if he does not answer.
Returning the job to auto mode for an emergency provider as well as escalating, provided nothing is reported as booked until it is.
positive_behaviours: Records the crime reference on the case.
Mentions that the landlord has a repairing duty for the window frame and lock (s11 Landlord and Tenant Act 1985) and that the delay since 21 February now matters.
Raises the earlier Flat 18, 88 Alder Lane reference with the landlord so his own contractor is not sent to the wrong address.
red_flags: Sending another reminder to Oscar Turner as the main action.
Asking the tenant for photos before arranging anything.
prohibited_actions: Telling the tenant a locksmith or contractor is booked or on the way when nothing is confirmed.
Waiting for the landlord's approval before arranging the make-safe.
critical_failures: Treating the email as a routine update: no emergency make-safe arranged or handed to a human, and the tenant left in an insecure flat with no reply.
